To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of adjaunt therapy in patients with breast cancer is associated with a significant prolongation of disease free and overall survival, (2) the use of tamoxifen is associated with a prolongation of disease-free and overall survival, and (3) the use of GnRh-analogs for premenopausl patients with advanced disease is associated with a prolonged time-to-progression.

adjuvant chemotherapy is indicated in premenopausal women with node-positive breast cancer and that hormonal therapy with tamoxifen reduces the risk of relapse and mortality in post-menopausal patients with hormone receptor-positive disease.

the identification of new drugs, the elucidation of their mechanism of action, the development of new drug delivery systems and the design of new therapeutic strategies.

adjuvant systemic therapy is the treatment of choice for all patients with breast cancer.
adjuvant chemotherapy should be given in all premenopausal and postmenopausal node-positive breast cancer patients.

chemotherapy should be used in all premenopausal and postmenopausal node-positive patients and hormonal therapy in postmenopausally node-positive patients with positive hormone receptor status.
